la:noun:anulus.html:
ānŭlus (not ann-), i, m.
2. anus, like circulus from circum, not a dim.
,
a ring, esp. for the finger, a finger-ring; and for sealing, a seal-ring, signet-ring.
Lit.: ille suum anulum opposuit,: de digito anulum Detraho,; ; et saep.; ; ; : (Gyges) anulum detraxit,: gemmatus,; ; ; et saep.: anulo tabulas obsignare,: sigilla anulo imprimere,; ; sqq. et saep.—The right to wear a gold ring was possessed, in the time of the Republic, only by the knights (equites); hence, equestris, * : anulum invenit = eques factus est,.—So also jus anulorum = dignitas equestris, : donatus anulo aureo,; so ; ; ; cf. Mayor ad ; Smith. Dict. Antiq.—
Of other articles in the form of rings.
A ring for curtains: velares anuli,. —
A link of a chain, ; cf. .—Irons for the feet, fetters: anulus cruribus aptus,.—
A curled lock of hair, a ringlet: comarum anulus,.—
A round ornament upon the capitals of Doric columns: anuli columnarum,.—
